anomalies.detail: peak Cp exceeds the Betz limit — likely nacelle anemometer bias, not real over-unity extraction

kelmarsh.explanation: Kelmarsh Wind Farm, comprising six turbines with a total capacity of 12.3 MW, has shown a minor discrepancy between actual and model-predicted power production over 8,174 hours, with actual output averaging 3.01 MW compared to a predicted 2.99 MW. The turbines' capacity factors range from 20.7% to 30.0%, with Kelmarsh_6 having the lowest at 20.7%, and Kelmarsh_5 the highest at 30.0%. The peak power coefficients (Cp) are close to the theoretical Betz limit of 0.593, with Kelmarsh_5 showing a peak Cp of 0.611, which suggests a potential anemometer calibration issue. Despite this, no visible blade damage was detected in Kelmarsh_6’s recent inspection. The recommendation to prioritize inspection of Kelmarsh_6 is supported by its lower capacity factor and the farm’s overall performance metrics.

recommendation.rationale: Kelmarsh_6 has the lowest capacity factor in the fleet (20.7% vs fleet mean 25.1%).

penmanshiel.explanation: Penmanshiel Wind Farm’s 14 turbines produced an average of 5.65 MW, closely matching the model prediction of 5.64 MW over 5,055 hours. Turbine capacity factors ranged from 21.6% to 31.6%, with a fleet mean of 26.0%. Penmanshiel_07, the lowest performer, has a capacity factor of 21.6% and a peak power coefficient of 0.512, below the Betz limit of 0.593, suggesting efficiency room. Blade inspections confirmed no damage. Despite no visible damage, Penmanshiel_07’s performance warrants further inspection. Historical data flagged turbine stop events and brake closures on other turbines, which may have impacted overall performance. These insights highlight the need to optimize turbine efficiency and address operational issues.

recommendation.rationale: Penmanshiel_07 has the lowest capacity factor in the fleet (21.6% vs fleet mean 26.0%).
